about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

accept.en: to agree to take or allow
accept.ex: The union refused to accept the offer.

according.ex: According to the report, prices fell last year.

accounts.en: a user's personal space on a website or app
accounts.ex: She opened a new email account yesterday.
accounts.zh: social media accounts：社群媒體帳號

acknowledged.ex: He acknowledged that the plan had problems.

act.en: to do something to deal with a problem
act.ex: The council must act before the bridge collapses.

activity.en: something people do, often for fun
activity.ex: Swimming is my favourite weekend activity.

added.ex: He added that the shop would open late.

addictive.en: making people want to keep using it
addictive.ex: Sugary snacks can be surprisingly addictive.

additionally.ex: Additionally, the hotel offers free parking.

advocates.en: publicly supports an idea or plan
advocates.ex: The doctor advocates daily exercise for everyone.

afterthought.en: something added later, not planned at first
afterthought.ex: The garden was added as an afterthought.

example.en: Parking was treated as an afterthought in the new stadium.
example.zh: 新體育場的停車設施只是事後才補上的。

note.meaning: 事後才想到或補加的東西，通常不被重視。
note.usage: 常見 as an afterthought（事後補上），帶有「沒有事先規劃、不夠重視」的負面意味。

noteEn.meaning: Something added later because nobody planned it at first.
noteEn.usage: Often 'as an afterthought'; it sounds negative.

noteEs.exampleTr: En el nuevo estadio, el aparcamiento fue una idea de último momento.
noteEs.meaning: Algo que se añade después, sin haberlo planeado.
noteEs.usage: Frase común: as an afterthought; tiene matiz negativo de falta de planificación.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए स्टेडियम में पार्किंग को बाद में सूझी बात की तरह लिया गया।
noteHi.meaning: बाद में सूझी या जोड़ी गई चीज़, जिसे ज़्यादा महत्व नहीं दिया गया।
noteHi.usage: आम वाक्यांश: as an afterthought; इसमें योजना की कमी का नकारात्मक भाव होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新スタジアムでは駐車場が後付けで扱われた。
noteJa.meaning: 後から思いついて付け足したもの。
noteJa.usage: as an afterthought の形が多く、「計画不足・軽視」という否定的な響きがある。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 경기장에서 주차장은 나중에 덧붙인 것처럼 취급되었다.
noteKo.usage: as an afterthought 형태가 흔하며, 계획 부족·경시의 부정적 뉘앙스가 있다.

afterthought.zh: as an afterthought：事後才補上的東西

age.ex: You must show proof of age to enter.

age-rating.en: a label saying what age something suits
age-rating.ex: Every video game carries an age-rating label.

agree.en: to have the same opinion; reach a deal
agree.ex: Both sides finally agreed on a new deal.

agreed.ex: The teachers agreed to change the timetable.

algorithmic.ex: Algorithmic feeds decide which posts you see.

almost.ex: The train was almost empty at midnight.

amplification.en: making something spread more or reach more people
amplification.ex: The amplification of fake news worries experts.

analogous.ex: The heart is analogous to a pump.

example.en: The brain is often seen as analogous to a computer.

note.usage: 正式用語，常接 to：be analogous to sth；名詞 analogy。

noteEn.meaning: Similar to something in some way.

noteEs.exampleTr: A menudo se considera el cerebro análogo a un ordenador.
noteEs.meaning: Parecido o comparable en algún aspecto.
noteEs.usage: Formal; suele ir con 'to': analogous to; el sustantivo es analogy.

noteHi.exampleTr: मस्तिष्क को अक्सर कंप्यूटर के समान माना जाता है।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; प्रायः 'analogous to' के साथ; संज्ञा analogy है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 脳はしばしばコンピューターに似たものと見なされる。
noteJa.usage: 硬い語で、analogous to ～ の形で使う。名詞は analogy。

noteKo.exampleTr: 뇌는 흔히 컴퓨터와 유사한 것으로 여겨진다.
noteKo.usage: 격식체이며 analogous to 형태로 쓴다. 명사는 analogy.

app.en: a program on a phone or computer
app.ex: I use an app to learn new words.

approach.en: a way of dealing with something
approach.ex: We need a new approach to this problem.

apps.en: programs on a phone or computer
apps.ex: My phone has too many apps.

argued.en: gave reasons to show something is true
argued.ex: He argued that the plan was too expensive.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

ask.ex: Let's ask the class for their opinions.

at.es: a (at the same rate: al mismo ritmo)
at.hi: पर (at the same rate: उसी दर पर)
at.ja: 〜で（at the same rate：同じ割合で）
at.zh: 以（at the same rate：以相同速度）

automatically.en: by itself, without a person doing it
automatically.ex: The door opens automatically when you approach.

autoplay.en: videos starting on their own one after another
autoplay.ex: I turned off autoplay on my phone.

back.ex: Most parents back the new school rules.

ban.ex: The city may ban cars from the centre.

barred.en: officially not allowed to do or have something
barred.ex: He was barred from the club for fighting.

battle.en: a hard struggle to achieve something
battle.ex: Losing weight can be a long battle.

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

behavioural.ex: The study looked at behavioural changes in teenagers.

blanket.en: covering everyone or everything, with no exceptions
blanket.ex: The city imposed a blanket ban on fireworks.

bodies.ex: Several public bodies support the plan.

bolted.en: added later in a quick, separate way
bolted.ex: Extra features were bolted on after launch.

built.ex: They plan to build more homes.

calls.ex: The union calls for higher wages.

central.ex: She played a central role in the project.

chair.en: the person in charge of a meeting or committee
chair.ex: She was elected chair of the board.

chairwoman.en: a woman who leads a committee or meeting
chairwoman.ex: The chairwoman opened the meeting at nine.

challenge.en: a difficult problem to deal with
challenge.ex: Finding staff is a big challenge for shops.

changes.ex: The new law brought many changes.

children.ex: Every child needs a safe place to play.

children's.ex: She works at a children's hospital.

choose.ex: Voters will choose a new mayor.

classification.en: putting things into groups by type or level
classification.ex: The classification of films helps parents choose.

coimisiún.en: Irish word for commission; part of regulator name
coimisiún.ja: コーミシューン（アイルランドのメディア委員会）
coimisiún.zh: Coimisiún na Meán：（愛爾蘭）媒體委員會

committee.en: a group chosen to do a task
committee.ex: The committee will decide next week.

companies.en: businesses that make or sell things
companies.ex: Many companies let staff work from home.

compelling.ex: The lawyer presented compelling proof of his innocence.

complete.ex: This book is a complete guide to Dublin.

comprising.ex: A team comprising five players won.

compulsory.ex: Wearing a seat belt is compulsory.

example.en: English is a compulsory subject in our school.
example.zh: 英語是我們學校的必修科目。

note.meaning: 必須做的；義務的、強制的。
note.usage: 常用於教育、法律：compulsory education/subject；反義詞 optional、voluntary。

noteEn.meaning: Something you must do because of a rule or law.
noteEn.usage: Common with education and laws, e.g. 'compulsory subject'; opposite is 'optional'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El inglés es una asignatura obligatoria en nuestra escuela.
noteEs.usage: Común en educación y leyes: compulsory education/subject; lo contrario es optional.

noteHi.exampleTr: हमारे स्कूल में अंग्रेज़ी एक अनिवार्य विषय है।
noteHi.usage: शिक्षा और कानून में आम: compulsory education/subject; विपरीत शब्द optional है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 英語は私たちの学校の必修科目だ。
noteJa.meaning: しなければならない、義務的な。
noteJa.usage: 教育や法律でよく使う：compulsory education/subject。反対語は optional。

noteKo.usage: 교육·법률에서 흔히 쓰임: compulsory education/subject. 반대말은 optional.

concluded.en: decided something after thinking about it
concluded.ex: The doctor concluded that he needed rest.

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerable.ex: The change saved a considerable amount of money.

contended.ex: She contended that the test was unfair.

content.ex: The website has lots of free content.

conventional.en: normal and usual; the standard type
conventional.ex: Conventional cars use petrol or diesel.

example.en: Electric cars are cheaper to run than conventional ones.
example.zh: 電動車的使用成本比傳統汽車低。

note.meaning: 傳統的、慣常的；一般標準的。
note.usage: 放在名詞前：conventional wisdom/methods/weapons；反義詞 unconventional、alternative。

noteEs.exampleTr: Los coches eléctricos son más baratos de usar que los convencionales.
noteEs.usage: Antes del sustantivo: conventional wisdom/methods; lo contrario es unconventional.

noteHi.exampleTr: इलेक्ट्रिक कारें चलाने में पारंपरिक कारों से सस्ती हैं।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले: conventional wisdom/methods; विपरीत unconventional है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 電気自動車は従来の車より維持費が安い。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前で使う：conventional wisdom/methods。反対語は unconventional。

noteKo.usage: 명사 앞에 쓴다: conventional wisdom/methods. 반대말은 unconventional.

cooperation.ex: Thanks for your cooperation with the survey.

cosgrove.en: family name of an Irish senator

deactivate.ex: You can deactivate your account at any time.

deactivation.en: the act of turning something off
deactivation.ex: Deactivation of the alarm needs a code.

deeming.en: judging or considering something to be
deeming.ex: They deemed the plan too risky.

default.en: the setting used unless you change it
default.ex: The phone is set to silent by default.

design.en: the way something is planned and made
design.ex: I love the design of this kitchen.

designed.en: planned and made to work a certain way
designed.ex: This chair was designed for comfort.

did.ex: Our team did well in the final.

difficult.ex: The test was difficult for everyone.

digital.ex: Many people now read digital books.

disable.ex: Please disable notifications during the exam.

disabled.en: turned off so it does not work
disabled.ex: The camera was disabled for privacy.

does.ex: He does his homework after dinner.
does.zh: 做；進行（does a survey：做調查）

drew.en: wrote or prepared a plan or list
drew.ex: The lawyer drew up a new contract.

embedded.en: made a fixed, basic part of something
embedded.ex: Respect is embedded in the school's culture.

example.en: Privacy should be embedded in every new product.
example.zh: 隱私保護應該融入每一項新產品之中。

note.meaning: 把某物牢固地嵌入或融入另一事物中，成為其基本部分。
note.usage: 常用被動：be embedded in/into sth；也可比喻觀念、文化根深蒂固。

noteEn.meaning: To put something firmly inside something else so it becomes part of it.

noteEs.exampleTr: La privacidad debería estar integrada en cada producto nuevo.
noteEs.meaning: Fijar o integrar algo firmemente dentro de otra cosa.
noteEs.usage: Frecuente en pasiva: be embedded in; también para ideas o culturas arraigadas.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर नए उत्पाद में गोपनीयता अंतर्निहित होनी चाहिए।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को दूसरी चीज़ में मज़बूती से जोड़ना या समाहित करना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर कर्मवाच्य: be embedded in; विचारों या संस्कृति के लिए भी प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: プライバシー保護はすべての新製品に組み込まれるべきだ。
noteJa.meaning: しっかりと組み込む、埋め込む。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be embedded in ～ が多い。考えや文化が根付いている意味にも使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 개인정보 보호는 모든 신제품에 내장되어야 한다.
noteKo.meaning: 어떤 것을 다른 것 안에 단단히 박아 넣거나 녹여 넣다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 수동태 be embedded in으로 쓰이며, 생각·문화가 뿌리내렸다는 뜻으로도 쓴다.

endless.ex: The kids asked endless questions on the trip.

endorsed.ex: The minister endorsed the new plan.

example.en: The union has endorsed the new pay deal.
example.zh: 工會已表態支持新的薪資協議。

note.meaning: 公開支持、認可（某人、計畫或產品）。
note.usage: 正式用語，後接名詞：endorse a plan/candidate/product；名詞為 endorsement。

noteEn.meaning: To say publicly that you support someone or something.

noteEs.exampleTr: El sindicato ha respaldado el nuevo acuerdo salarial.
noteEs.meaning: Apoyar o aprobar públicamente algo o a alguien.
noteEs.usage: Formal; va seguido de sustantivo: endorse a plan/candidate; el sustantivo es endorsement.

noteHi.exampleTr: यूनियन ने नए वेतन समझौते का समर्थन किया है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी व्यक्ति, योजना या उत्पाद का सार्वजनिक समर्थन करना।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; सीधे संज्ञा के साथ: endorse a plan/candidate; संज्ञा रूप endorsement है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 組合は新しい賃金協定を支持した。
noteJa.meaning: （人・計画・商品を）公に支持・承認する。
noteJa.usage: 硬い表現で、直接目的語をとる：endorse a plan/candidate。名詞は endorsement。

noteKo.usage: 격식체이며 목적어를 바로 취한다: endorse a plan/candidate. 명사형은 endorsement.

endorsing.ex: The minister is endorsing the new health plan.

example.en: The union has endorsed the new pay deal.
example.zh: 工會已表態支持新的薪資協議。

note.meaning: 公開支持、認可（某人、計畫或產品）。
note.usage: 正式用語，後接名詞：endorse a plan/candidate/product；名詞為 endorsement。

noteEn.meaning: To say publicly that you support someone or something.

noteEs.exampleTr: El sindicato ha respaldado el nuevo acuerdo salarial.
noteEs.meaning: Apoyar o aprobar públicamente algo o a alguien.
noteEs.usage: Formal; va seguido de sustantivo: endorse a plan/candidate; el sustantivo es endorsement.

noteHi.exampleTr: यूनियन ने नए वेतन समझौते का समर्थन किया है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी व्यक्ति, योजना या उत्पाद का सार्वजनिक समर्थन करना।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; सीधे संज्ञा के साथ: endorse a plan/candidate; संज्ञा रूप endorsement है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 組合は新しい賃金協定を支持した。
noteJa.meaning: （人・計画・商品を）公に支持・承認する。
noteJa.usage: 硬い表現で、直接目的語をとる：endorse a plan/candidate。名詞は endorsement。

noteKo.usage: 격식체이며 목적어를 바로 취한다: endorse a plan/candidate. 명사형은 endorsement.

evidence.en: something that shows a thing is true
evidence.ex: The new jobs are evidence that the town is growing.

example.en: something that shows what you mean
example.ex: Fruit, for example apples, is good for you.

existing.ex: We will improve the existing system.

fact.ex: In fact, the test was easy.

far.ex: This is far better than the old version.
far.ja: はるかに（far from：決して〜ない）
syn: a lot (far from: not at all)

faster.ex: Prices are rising faster than wages.

features.en: parts or functions of a product
features.ex: This phone has many useful features.

films.ex: We watched two films last weekend.

firms.ex: Tech firms are hiring more engineers.

follows.ex: The strike follows weeks of failed talks.

forthcoming.ex: The forthcoming election is in May.

example.en: Details will be announced at the forthcoming meeting.
example.zh: 細節將在即將召開的會議上公布。

note.meaning: 即將到來的、即將發生或發表的。
note.usage: 放在名詞前：forthcoming election/book/law；放在名詞後或 be 動詞後時意為「提供的、願意透露的」。

noteEn.usage: Usually before a noun: 'the forthcoming election'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los detalles se anunciarán en la próxima reunión.
noteEs.meaning: Que va a llegar u ocurrir pronto; próximo.
noteEs.usage: Antes del sustantivo: forthcoming election/book; 'be forthcoming' también significa 'dispuesto a dar información'.

noteHi.exampleTr: विवरण आगामी बैठक में घोषित किए जाएँगे।
noteHi.meaning: जल्द आने वाला या होने वाला।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा से पहले: forthcoming election/book; 'be forthcoming' का अर्थ 'जानकारी देने को तैयार' भी होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 詳細は今度の会議で発表される。
noteJa.meaning: 近く行われる、まもなく出る。
noteJa.usage: 名詞の前に置く：forthcoming election/book。be forthcoming は「協力的・率直な」の意味にもなる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 세부 사항은 다가오는 회의에서 발표될 것이다.
noteKo.usage: 명사 앞에 쓴다: forthcoming election/book. be forthcoming은 '기꺼이 알려 주는'의 뜻도 있다.

frameworks.ex: The law provides a framework for online safety.

garda.en: the national police force of Ireland
garda.ja: ガルダ（アイルランド警察）

gardaí.en: Irish police officers; the Irish police
gardaí.ja: ガルダイ（アイルランド警察）

get.en: to persuade someone to do something
get.ex: I can't get my son to eat vegetables.

giants.ex: Oil giants made huge profits this year.

governing.ex: The governing body meets once a month.

group.en: a number of people or things together
group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

groups.en: organisations of people with shared interests
groups.ex: Several community groups joined the protest.

had.en: possessed; was involved (had a hand in)
had.ex: She had a key role in the project.

hard.ex: It is hard to wake up early in winter.

harmful.ex: Smoking is harmful to your health.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

hearing.en: receiving views or information from people
hearing.ex: We look forward to hearing from you.

hearings.en: official meetings where people give their views
hearings.ex: Public hearings on the plan start next week.

hold.ex: Fear began to take hold of the crowd.

hooks.en: makes someone very attracted or addicted
hooks.ex: The first chapter hooks every reader.

host.ex: The town offers a host of activities for kids.

however.ex: It was sunny; however, it was cold.

ideas.ex: Send us your ideas for the party.

informed.ex: Our decision was informed by public feedback.

integrated.en: made part of something from the start
integrated.ex: Solar panels are integrated into the roof.

internet.ex: I found the recipe on the internet.

issue.ex: Housing is a major issue for young people.

keep.en: to make someone stay in a state or place
keep.ex: Coffee keeps me awake at night.

keeps.en: makes someone stay in a state or place
keeps.ex: Good music keeps me happy while I work.

keogh.en: family name of an Irish politician

kids.en: part of the name 'EU Kids Act'
kids.zh: EU Kids Act：歐盟兒童法案

later.ex: We can talk about it later.

law.ex: Wearing a seat belt is the law.

least.ex: You should, at the very least, say sorry.

longer.ex: The talks were long and difficult.

maintained.ex: He maintains that the plan will work.

make.ex: The change will make life easier.

mandating.ex: The law is mandating helmets for all cyclists.

mandatory.ex: Safety training is mandatory for new staff.

example.en: Wearing a helmet is mandatory on building sites.
example.zh: 在工地戴安全帽是強制規定。

note.meaning: 依法律或規定必須做的；強制性的。
note.usage: 多用於正式語境，常見 mandatory for sb、it is mandatory to do；語氣比 compulsory 更正式、偏法規。

noteEn.meaning: Required by a law or rule; you must do it.
noteEn.usage: Formal word; often 'it is mandatory to do something' or 'mandatory for someone'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Llevar casco es obligatorio en las obras.
noteEs.meaning: Obligatorio por ley o por norma.
noteEs.usage: Registro formal; se usa en 'mandatory for alguien' o 'it is mandatory to...'.

noteHi.exampleTr: निर्माण स्थलों पर हेलमेट पहनना अनिवार्य है।
noteHi.meaning: कानून या नियम के अनुसार अनिवार्य।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक भाषा में; 'mandatory for someone' या 'it is mandatory to...' के रूप में आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 建設現場ではヘルメットの着用が義務付けられている。
noteJa.meaning: 法律や規則で義務付けられている。
noteJa.usage: 公式な文脈で使う。mandatory for 人／it is mandatory to do の形が多い。

noteKo.meaning: 법이나 규정에 의해 반드시 해야 하는.
noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 표현으로, mandatory for 사람 / it is mandatory to do 형태로 자주 쓰인다.

material.en: content such as text, images or video
material.ex: The site removed violent material quickly.

media.en: TV, radio, newspapers and the internet

meeting.en: an event where people gather to talk

meán.en: Irish word for media; part of regulator name
meán.zh: Coimisiún na Meán：（愛爾蘭）媒體委員會

modelled.en: designed to copy or follow something
modelled.ex: The new park is modelled on Central Park.

moving.ex: The police are moving quickly on the case.

much.ex: The new phone is much faster.

na.en: Irish word meaning 'of the'; part of a name
na.ja: ナ（アイルランド語の冠詞）
na.zh: Coimisiún na Meán（愛爾蘭語冠詞）

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

new.ex: The city opened a new library.

normal.ex: It was a normal day at school.

off.ex: All her hard work finally paid off.

on.en: used in 'pass on' = give to someone else
on.ex: Please pass the message on to your sister.

online.ex: Teenagers spend hours online every day.

outpacing.en: moving or growing faster than something else
outpacing.ex: Prices are outpacing wages this year.

example.en: Demand for housing continues to outpace supply.
example.zh: 住房需求持續超過供給。

paragraphs: A group of politicians wrote a report about children and the internet. It has 45 ideas.
The report says some app features keep children online too long. One example is endless scrolling. Another is videos that play by themselves.
The report says these features should be off at the start. Companies should not turn them on for children.
The report does not ask for a full ban on social media for under-16s. But it says children under 13 should not have normal social media accounts.
The chair, Keira Keogh, said apps must be safe from the start. She said companies can turn these features off quickly.

Apps and websites should turn off features that make children use them too much, a new report says. The Oireachtas Committee on Children wrote the report after meeting teachers, young people, the Gardaí, the online safety regulator and tech companies. It has 45 recommendations.

The report wants a law to switch off features like endless scrolling, videos that play automatically, and systems that push harmful content. It also suggests age ratings for all digital products, like the ratings for toys and films.

The committee said a total ban on social media for under-16s probably would not solve the problem. But it agreed that children under 13 should not have normal social media accounts, as the EU has suggested.

Committee chair Keira Keogh said technology changes faster than the rules, so safety must be built in from the start. She said endless scrolling keeps children online much longer than they want, and companies could turn it off very quickly.
Labour senator Nessa Cosgrove said it will be hard to get tech companies to agree.

Addictive features on apps and websites should be disabled by default for children, according to a report by the Oireachtas Committee on Children. The report, which contains 45 recommendations, follows hearings with youth and teacher groups, the Garda, the regulator Coimisiún na Meán and several tech companies.

It calls for legislation requiring platforms to switch off features such as infinite scroll, autoplay, the algorithmic promotion of harmful content and behavioural profiling. It also proposes a mandatory age classification system for all digital products, similar to those already used for toys and films.

The committee concluded that a blanket ban on social media for under-16s was unlikely to provide a complete solution. However, it welcomed the planned EU Kids Act and agreed that, at a minimum, children under 13 should not hold standard social media accounts.

Committee chairwoman Keira Keogh said technology was moving faster than regulation, so safety had to be designed in from the start rather than added later. Infinite scroll, she said, keeps children online far longer than they would like, and companies could turn it off very quickly.
Labour senator Nessa Cosgrove warned that persuading tech firms to accept this approach would be difficult.

Addictive design features on apps and websites should be switched off by default, an Oireachtas committee has urged in a wide-ranging report on children's online safety. The Committee on Children drew up its 45 recommendations after hearing from youth and teacher bodies, the Garda, the media regulator Coimisiún na Meán and a host of tech firms.

Central to the report is a call for legislation compelling platforms to disable infinite scroll, autoplay, the algorithmic amplification of harmful material and behavioural profiling. It also advocates a compulsory age-rating regime for digital products, modelled on those governing toys and films.

The committee stopped short of endorsing a blanket social media ban for under-16s, deeming it unlikely to be a panacea. It did, however, back the forthcoming EU Kids Act and agreed that under-13s should, at the very least, be barred from conventional social media accounts.

Its chairwoman, Keira Keogh, argued that regulation was struggling to keep pace with technology, so safety had to be embedded by design rather than bolted on as an afterthought. Infinite scroll, she said, hooks children far beyond what they would choose, yet firms could disable it almost overnight.
Labour senator Nessa Cosgrove cautioned that winning over the tech giants would be an uphill battle.

Addictive features on digital platforms should be disabled by default, according to a comprehensive report on children's online safety published by the Oireachtas Committee on Children. The report, comprising 45 recommendations, was informed by evidence from youth and teacher organisations, the Garda, the regulator Coimisiún na Meán and numerous technology companies.

Principally, it recommends legislation mandating the deactivation of infinite scroll, autoplay, the algorithmic amplification of harmful content and behavioural profiling. Additionally, it proposes a mandatory age classification system for digital products, analogous to existing frameworks for toys and films.

The committee concluded that a comprehensive ban on social media for under-16s would be unlikely to resolve the issue. Nevertheless, it endorsed the proposed EU Kids Act and maintained that, at a minimum, children under 13 should be prohibited from holding conventional social media accounts.

The committee chairwoman, Keira Keogh, contended that technological development is outpacing regulation; consequently, safety must be integrated at the design stage rather than considered retrospectively. She emphasised that infinite scroll substantially prolongs children's online activity, despite the fact that companies could deactivate it rapidly.
However, Labour senator Nessa Cosgrove acknowledged that securing the cooperation of technology companies would present a considerable challenge.
